children: shares were unchanged in Copenhagen after the company signed a global exclusive license and collaboration deal worth up to 1.165 billion ($1.3 billion) with Nanexa, a Swedish drug delivery company. Nanexa's Stockholm-listed shares more than doubled in early Friday trading.

The deal gives Novo rights to PharmaShell, Nanexa's platform that coats individual drug particles in an ultra-thin inorganic layer to release them slowly, for certain peptide drugs in obesity, type 2 diabetes and other cardiometabolic diseases. The aim is long-acting injectables that could reduce dosing frequency. Of the total, 615 million comes from an upfront payment plus development and regulatory milestones, with the rest tied to sales milestones. Nanexa will also receive low single-digit royalties, and Novo will lead development and commercialization.
The companies already worked together under a 2022 PharmaShell deal, and Nanexa's chairman, Goran Ando, sat on Novo's board from 2005 to 2018, the last five years as chairman.

title: Novo Pays Up to $1.3 Billion for Nanexa's Drug Delivery Tech
